revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega’s Treasure Square
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega buried treasure at the four corners of a square. Three corners are at (2, 2), (2, 6), and (6, 6). She always plots her corners in Quadrant I. What ordered pair is the fourth corner, and what is the side length of the square?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The fourth corner is (6, 2). The square has a side length of 4 units, because from (2, 2) to (6, 2) is 6 − 2 = 4 units and from (2, 2) to (2, 6) is 6 − 2 = 4 units.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do you plot a point on the coordinate plane?
conceptIntro.intro: An ordered pair (x, y) is two numbers that tell you exactly where a point goes. The first number moves you right or left. The second number moves you up or down. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Always start at the origin (0, 0), move right/left first, then up/down.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I will plot the point (5, 4). The 5 is the x-coordinate, and the 4 is the y-coordinate.
I start at the origin, which is (0, 0).
First I move 5 units to the right along the x-axis.
Then I move 4 units up. I place my dot. That is the point (5, 4).

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's plot (2, 1). Where do we start? At the origin (0, 0).
How far do we move right? The first number is 2, so we move 2 right.
How far do we move up? The second number is 1, so we move 1 up and place the dot.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.
Remember the key idea: Always start at the origin (0, 0), move right/left first, then up/down..

explore.instructions: Quick warm-up together: Plot Captain Vega's treasure map points and connect them to reveal the path!
explore.label: Plot the three treasure map waypoints.

discourse.prompt: You plotted a triangle. How did the ordered pairs tell you exactly where to place each point?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The first number in the ordered pair tells me ___ and the second number tells me ___. The point (5, 4) means ___.

approaching.stem: Which ordered pair names a point 3 units right and 7 units up from the origin?
approaching.explanation: The first coordinate is horizontal (right 3), the second is vertical (up 7). So (3, 7).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Re-read the moves: 3 units right, then 7 units up. Which move comes first in an ordered pair?
An ordered pair is (x, y): x is the right/left distance, y is the up/down distance. Match each move to its slot.
Start at the origin and go right 3 — that 3 is the x, the first number. Now decide where the 'up 7' goes.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué par ordenado nombra un punto que está 3 unidades a la derecha y 7 unidades hacia arriba desde el origen?
approaching.explanationEs: La primera coordenada es horizontal (3 a la derecha) y la segunda es vertical (7 hacia arriba). Entonces (3, 7).

approaching.stem: What are the coordinates of the origin?
approaching.explanation: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis cross, at (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: The origin is where both axes cross, where both values are zero.
Both coordinates at the origin are 0 — not mixed with 1.
Check both the x and y values at the origin.
hints: The origin is the exact spot where the x-axis and y-axis cross. Picture that crossing point.
Ask: how far right have you moved at the origin? How far up? Those two distances are the coordinates.
At the crossing point you haven't moved right at all, so x = 0. Now figure out the y-value the same way.
approaching.explanationEs: El origen es donde se cruzan el eje x y el eje y, en (0, 0).

approaching.stem: A point is at (6, 2). What does the 6 tell you?
approaching.explanation: The first number (x-coordinate) tells you horizontal movement. 6 means go right 6 units from the origin.
choiceFeedback: The first number controls horizontal movement—check which number moves you up.
With a positive first number, you move right—not left.
Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: In (6, 2), the 6 is the FIRST number. First and second positions have different jobs.
First number = x = horizontal (right/left). Second number = y = vertical (up/down). Positive means right or up.
The 6 sits in the x spot and it's positive, so it describes a horizontal move. Which direction is positive x?
approaching.stemEs: Un punto está en (6, 2). ¿Qué te indica el 6?
approaching.explanationEs: El primer número (la coordenada x) indica el movimiento horizontal. El 6 significa avanzar 6 unidades a la derecha desde el origen.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Move up
workedExample.work: Move 5 units UP along the y-axis.

workedExample.label: Move right
workedExample.work: Move 2 units to the right. Place the dot at (2, 5).

approaching.correctWork: The student moved UP first. The FIRST number (5) is the x-coordinate, so move 5 units RIGHT; then the SECOND number (2) is the y-coordinate, so move 2 units UP. The point is (5, 2), not (2, 5).
hints: Which direction does the first number in (x, y) tell you to move — right or up?
The first number is always the horizontal (right) move. Here that is 5 right, then 2 up.
approaching.explanation: The first number of an ordered pair is always the x-coordinate, which is a horizontal move. Here the 5 should send you 5 units RIGHT, and then the 2 sends you 2 units UP. Moving up first swaps the coordinates and lands on (2, 5), a completely different point from (5, 2).
approaching.explanationEs: El primer número de un par ordenado siempre es la coordenada x, que es un movimiento horizontal. Aquí el 5 debe llevarte 5 unidades a la DERECHA, y después el 2 te lleva 2 unidades hacia ARRIBA. Moverse primero hacia arriba intercambia las coordenadas y cae en (2, 5), un punto totalmente distinto de (5, 2).

approaching.stem: Spot 1 — Captain Vega's first clue says the Sandy Dock is right 7 and up 2 from the origin. Which ordered pair names the Sandy Dock?
approaching.explanation: The x-coordinate is the sideways move (right 7) and the y-coordinate is the up move (up 2), so the Sandy Dock is (7, 2).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
approaching.stemEs: Punto 1: la primera pista de la capitana Vega dice que el Muelle de Arena está 7 a la derecha y 2 hacia arriba desde el origen. ¿Qué par ordenado nombra el Muelle de Arena?
approaching.explanationEs: La coordenada x es el movimiento hacia los lados (7 a la derecha) y la coordenada y es el movimiento hacia arriba (2 hacia arriba), así que el Muelle de Arena es (7, 2).
hints: An ordered pair is always written (x, y): the sideways number first, the up-and-down number second.
Match each clue word to a coordinate — “right” describes the x-coordinate and “up” describes the y-coordinate.
The clue says right 7, so 7 belongs in the first position. Now decide which number goes in the second position.
hintsEs: Un par ordenado siempre se escribe (x, y): primero el número hacia los lados y después el número hacia arriba o abajo.
Relaciona cada palabra de la pista con una coordenada: «a la derecha» describe la coordenada x y «hacia arriba» describe la coordenada y.
La pista dice 7 a la derecha, así que el 7 va en la primera posición. Ahora decide qué número va en la segunda posición.

approaching.stem: Spot 2 — The map marks the Lookout Tower at (4, 9). What does the 4 tell you to do from the origin?
choices: Move 4 units to the right along the x-axis
Move 4 units up along the y-axis
approaching.explanation: The first number in (x, y) is the x-coordinate, so 4 means move 4 units to the right along the x-axis before moving up.
choiceFeedback: The first number controls horizontal movement—check which number moves you up.
With a positive first number, you move right—not left.
Staying on the y-axis would mean the x-coordinate is 0. Here the first number is 4, and the first number controls sideways movement.
approaching.stemEs: Punto 2: el mapa marca la Torre de Vigía en (4, 9). ¿Qué te indica hacer el 4 desde el origen?
approaching.explanationEs: El primer número de (x, y) es la coordenada x, así que el 4 significa moverse 4 unidades a la derecha sobre el eje x antes de subir.
hints: In an ordered pair, the first number always describes movement along the x-axis.
Start at the origin and think about which axis you travel along before you go up.
In (4, 9) the 4 is the x-coordinate, so it controls the sideways move — now decide whether that move goes right or left from the origin.
hintsEs: En un par ordenado, el primer número siempre describe el movimiento sobre el eje x.
Empieza en el origen y piensa sobre qué eje te desplazas antes de subir.
En (4, 9) el 4 es la coordenada x, así que controla el movimiento hacia los lados; ahora decide si ese movimiento va a la derecha o a la izquierda desde el origen.

onLevel.stem: Spot 3 — Vega writes: 'The Coconut Grove is 3 across and 8 up.' Which point on the map is the Coconut Grove?
onLevel.explanation: Across (3) is the x-coordinate and up (8) is the y-coordinate, so the Coconut Grove is at (3, 8).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
The first number fits the “across” clue, but the second number repeats it instead of coming from the “up” part of the clue.
Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
onLevel.stemEs: Punto 3: Vega escribe: 'El Cocotal está 3 a lo ancho y 8 hacia arriba'. ¿Qué punto del mapa es el Cocotal?
onLevel.explanationEs: A lo ancho (3) es la coordenada x y hacia arriba (8) es la coordenada y, así que el Cocotal está en (3, 8).
hints: “Across” and “up” are the two directions an ordered pair records, and it records them in that order.
Write the across number first and the up number second, exactly the way (x, y) is set up.
The clue gives 3 across, so 3 belongs in the first position — now check which choice also uses the up number in the second position.
hintsEs: «A lo ancho» y «hacia arriba» son las dos direcciones que registra un par ordenado, y las registra en ese orden.
Escribe primero el número a lo ancho y después el número hacia arriba, tal como está formado (x, y).
La pista da 3 a lo ancho, así que el 3 va en la primera posición; ahora revisa qué opción también usa el número hacia arriba en la segunda posición.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Captain Vega's Misread Coordinate

workedExample.label: Read the x-coordinate
workedExample.work: Move 3 units to the right along the x-axis.

workedExample.label: Read the y-coordinate
workedExample.work: Move 1 unit up along the y-axis.

workedExample.label: Plot the point
workedExample.work: Place the flag where (3, 1) would go.

onLevel.correctWork: The x move is correct (3 right), but the y-coordinate is 6, not 1. The navigator should move 6 units up, placing the flag at (3, 6) — not (3, 1).
hints: Look at the SECOND number in (3, 6). How many units up should the flag move?
y = 6, so move 6 units up after the 3 right. The point is (3, 6), not (3, 1).
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: la coordenada mal leída del capitán Vega
onLevel.explanation: The x move is right: 3 units across. The mistake is the y move — the second number in (3, 6) is 6, not 1, so the flag should rise 6 units after the 3 right. Placing it at (3, 1) puts the Pirate Flag five units too low.
onLevel.explanationEs: El movimiento en x está bien: 3 unidades a la derecha. El error está en el movimiento en y: el segundo número de (3, 6) es 6, no 1, así que la bandera debe subir 6 unidades después de las 3 a la derecha. Colocarla en (3, 1) deja la bandera pirata cinco unidades demasiado abajo.

onLevel.title: Miscounted Grid Lines

workedExample.label: Move along the x-axis
workedExample.work: Start at the origin (0, 0) and count 7 units to the right.

workedExample.label: Move along the y-axis
workedExample.work: Count up from the x-axis: 1, 2, 3, 4 — stop on 4.

onLevel.correctWork: The x-axis itself is 0, not 1. Counting up correctly: 1, 2, 3 — the third count lands on y = 3, so the point is (7, 3), not (7, 4). The student started counting one gridline too high by treating the x-axis as unit 1 instead of unit 0.
hints: When you count up from the x-axis, is the x-axis itself unit 0 or unit 1?
The x-axis is 0. The first line above it is 1, the second is 2, the third is 3. So 3 units up lands on y = 3, not y = 4.
onLevel.titleEs: Líneas de la cuadrícula mal contadas
onLevel.explanation: Counting up has to start with the x-axis as 0, not 1. The first line above the x-axis is 1, the second is 2, and the third is 3, so 3 units up lands on y = 3. Treating the axis itself as unit 1 pushes every count one gridline too high, which is how (7, 3) turned into (7, 4).
onLevel.explanationEs: Al contar hacia arriba hay que tomar el eje x como 0, no como 1. La primera línea arriba del eje x es 1, la segunda es 2 y la tercera es 3, así que 3 unidades hacia arriba caen en y = 3. Tratar el eje mismo como la unidad 1 corre toda la cuenta una línea de más, y así (7, 3) se convirtió en (7, 4).

onLevel.prompt: A student says that (3, 5) and (5, 3) are the same point because they use the same numbers. Is the student correct? Explain why or why not, and describe where each point is located on the coordinate plane.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because (3, 5) means ___ while (5, 3) means ___. The ORDER matters because ___.
onLevel.hint: Compare what each coordinate pair tells you about horizontal and vertical moves.
hints: Both pairs use 3 and 5, but look at which number sits in the x (first) spot in each pair.
Describe each point's moves separately: (3, 5) = right ?, up ?; (5, 3) = right ?, up ?. Compare the two paths.
First step: for (3, 5), go right 3 and up 5. Now do (5, 3)'s moves and check whether you land on the same dot.
onLevel.explanation: The student is not correct. In (3, 5) the 3 is the x-coordinate, so you move right 3 and up 5, landing high and toward the left. In (5, 3) the 5 is the x-coordinate, so you move right 5 and up 3, landing lower and farther right. Same digits, different jobs — the order inside an ordered pair decides which direction each number controls.
onLevel.explanationEs: El estudiante no tiene razón. En (3, 5) el 3 es la coordenada x, así que te mueves 3 a la derecha y 5 hacia arriba, y caes alto y hacia la izquierda. En (5, 3) el 5 es la coordenada x, así que te mueves 5 a la derecha y 3 hacia arriba, y caes más abajo y más a la derecha. Los mismos dígitos, distintas funciones: el orden dentro del par ordenado decide qué dirección controla cada número.

onLevel.label: Put these steps in order for plotting the point (4, 5).
items: Move 4 units to the right along the x-axis
Move 5 units up from that spot
Place a dot at the point (4, 5)
correctOrder: Move 4 units to the right along the x-axis
Move 5 units up from that spot
Place a dot at the point (4, 5)
onLevel.hint: Start with the first step: where do you always begin when plotting?
hints: Every plotting routine begins at the same home spot before any moving happens.
Think: start point, then horizontal move, then vertical move, then mark the dot. Order the cards to tell that story.
Place 'Start at the origin (0, 0)' first. Then ask: does the 4 (x) move or the 5 (y) move come next?
onLevel.explanation: Plotting always begins at the origin (0, 0), because every ordered pair counts its moves from there. The first number, 4, is the x-coordinate, so the move right along the x-axis comes next; the second number, 5, is the y-coordinate, so the move up follows; then you mark the dot at (4, 5).
onLevel.explanationEs: Ubicar un punto siempre empieza en el origen (0, 0), porque todo par ordenado cuenta sus movimientos desde ahí. El primer número, 4, es la coordenada x, así que sigue el movimiento hacia la derecha sobre el eje x; el segundo número, 5, es la coordenada y, así que después va el movimiento hacia arriba; y por último marcas el punto en (4, 5).

onLevel.label: Match each ordered pair to its description.
onLevel.hint: Try the first step of the solution process.
hints: Each pair is (x, y): first number = right, second = up. A 0 means you don't move in that direction.
Translate each pair into moves, like (4, 2) = right 4, up 2. Pairs with a 0 in them land ON an axis.
Try (3, 0): right 3, up 0 — you never leave the x-axis. Use that same test on (0, 4) and the rest.
onLevel.explanation: Every ordered pair is (x, y): the first number is the move right and the second is the move up. So (4, 2) is right 4, up 2; (1, 6) is right 1, up 6; and (5, 5) is right 5, up 5. A 0 means no movement in that direction — (3, 0) never leaves the x-axis, (0, 4) never leaves the y-axis, and (0, 0) is the origin where the two axes meet.
onLevel.explanationEs: Todo par ordenado es (x, y): el primer número es el movimiento hacia la derecha y el segundo es el movimiento hacia arriba. Así, (4, 2) es derecha 4, arriba 2; (1, 6) es derecha 1, arriba 6; y (5, 5) es derecha 5, arriba 5. Un 0 significa que no hay movimiento en esa dirección: (3, 0) nunca deja el eje x, (0, 4) nunca deja el eje y, y (0, 0) es el origen, donde se cruzan los dos ejes.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Graph on the Coordinate Plane is swapping the order of the coordinates — moving up/down first instead of right/left first. For example, when plotting (5, 2), students often move up 5 and right 2, landing on the wrong point (2, 5) instead of (5, 2). Remember: the x-coordinate (first number) always tells you how far to move right or left along the x-axis; the y-coordinate (second number) tells you how far up or down along the y-axis.

optionalActivity.name: Coordinate Treasure Map
optionalActivity.intro: Optional — one more together if the group is ready: Read Captain Vega's ordered-pair clues to plot every treasure spot in Quadrant I.

diagram.title: Drone Flight Path Triangle
diagram.caption: Each ordered pair (x, y) places a stop: read x for the sideways move, y for the up move — connect Base to Pickup to Delivery and back to see the triangle.

connect.scenario: A drone delivery company programs flight paths using coordinate pairs. A drone starts at the warehouse (0, 0), flies to pickup at (3, 6), then delivers to (8, 2), then returns to base (0, 0).
connect.promptQuestion: How do ordered pairs help the drone navigate? What shape does the flight path make?
connect.prompt: The drone uses ordered pairs because the first number controls ___ movement and the second controls ___. The path makes a ___ shape.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Point P is located 6 units right and 3 units up from the origin. What ordered pair names point P?
exitTicket.explanation: Right 6 = x-coordinate of 6, Up 3 = y-coordinate of 3. The ordered pair is (6, 3).

questions.stem: A data set is symmetric. What is likely true about the mean and median?
choices: The mean is much higher than the median
The median is much higher than the mean
They are always exactly the same
questions.explanation: In a symmetric distribution, the mean and median are approximately equal because the data is balanced on both sides.

questions.stem: A histogram of basketball players' ages shows: most players are 22–28, with a long tail of older players up to age 40. What is the shape of this distribution?
questions.explanation: Most data is on the left (younger ages) with a tail stretching right (older ages). This is skewed right.

questions.stem: Which word describes the direction of the TAIL, not the peak?
choices: Skew — the direction of the long tail tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction of the peak tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction the median points
Skew — the direction of the mode
questions.explanation: The skew direction is named after the TAIL. If the tail stretches to the right, it is skewed right, even though the peak is on the left.
